p: As you enter Route 11 from Route 12 to the east, head north at the end of the northern fence. You'll find a Berry Tree which yields 10 Grepa Berries. Just east of the fence below the berry tree is Youngster Owen in the grass, he has a Lv 55 Arcanine. To the north is Psychic Fidel who has a Lv 54 Xatu. Continue west from Fidel to find Youngster Jason who has a Lv 55 Octillery and a Lv 55 Crobat. Continue west a bit further to find Psychich Herman in some grass, he has a Lv 55 Exeggutor, a Lv 55 Xatu, and a Lv 55 Starmie. Return to Route 12 to the east and follow the boardwalk north. This will eventually land you in Lavender Town!

wt.title: Lavender Town
p: As you enter Lavender Town from Route 12 to the South, the first house you see to the west is the residence of another Name Rater. The large building in town is the Kanto Radio Tower. Speaking to NPC's in here will reveal that the Power Plant is experiencing issues, clueing us to our next objective. Heal up at the Pokécenter and head north out of town towards Route 10.

wt.title: Route 10 South
p: As you enter Route 10 from Lavender Town to the south, head north, east, and then north through two gaps between ledges to battle Hiker Jim who has a Lv 58 Machamp. Go north one step, and then head west to battle Pokefan Robert who has a Lv 60 Kangaskhan. To the west you'll find an Ultra Ball. Enter the cave opening to the north to reach the Rock Tunnel.

wt.title: Rock Tunnel
p:
As you enter the tunnel from Route 10 to the south, head north into a wall, then head west to find an Elixer. Head east until you hit a wall, south until you hit a wall, and then east to find TM42 (Facade). Head north and descend the ladder up ahead.
 On the next floor, head south, east at the branch in the path, south at the next branch as far down as you can go, and then west to find a PP Up. Head back east, north, east at the branch in the path, north as far as you can go, and then east to find an Iron. Head back west, south, and then east at the branch in the path. Ascend the ladder.
 On the next floor, head south as far as you can go, sixteen steps west, and then north until you reach a ladder that you will descend.
 On the next floor, head south as far as you can go, five steps east, south as far as you can go, nine steps west, south as far as you can go, twelve steps west, six steps south, twenty-one steps east, and then north to a ladder that you will ascend.
 On the final floor, head south as far as you can go, west as far as you can go, north as far as you can go, and then finally ascend the ladder you see to the west to exit the Rock Tunnel.

wt.title: Route 10 North/Power Plant
p:
As you enter Route 10 from the Rock Tunnel, you'll see a Pokécenter to the east. Heal up if needed, and then head north from the Pokécenter, through a gap in a ledge and into some grass. Head west and then north through a gap in the fence and to a coastline. Surf east into a wall, and then south until you see some land to disembark on to the west. Follow this land south and then west to find the Power Plant!
 Just outside is Leader LT Surge, speak to him to send him to the Fighting Dojo in Saffron where you can challenge him to a rematch. Enter the Power Plant and make your way through an opening in the wall to the northeast. In the next room, speak to the scientist NPC in front of a generator. He will reveal himself to be the manager and talk about how someone ruined his generator. 
 Return to the entrance of the Power Plant. As you try to exit, a security guard will stop and ask you to investigate a shady character in Cerulean City. Our next objective is clear, surf back to northern part of Route 10 and take the path just west of the tall grass which leads to Route 9.

wt.title: Route 9
p:
As you enter Route 9 from Route 10 to the east, walk east until you hit a wall. Jump a ledge just below you to battle Picnicker Heidi, she has a Lv 56 Jumpluff and a Lv 58 Seadra. Jump another ledge to the south to battle Hiker TIm who has a Lv 55 Golem, a Lv 55 Kabutops, and a Lv 55 Quagsire. Head west and then north through a gap between ledges. Head east, north through a gap between a ledge and a cliff, and then north through a gap between two ledges to battle Hiker Sidney. Sidney has a Lv 56 Dugtrio and a Lv 56 Steelix. Head back south between the ledges, west at the first branch in the path, and then south to battle Picnicker Edna who has a Lv 56 Nidoqueen and a Lv 56 Raichu. 
 Jump the ledge to the south and then head west to battle Camper Dean who has a Lv 56 Heracross and a Lv 57 Kangaskhan. Head back east a short distance, and then north through a gap between a ledge and a cliff. Continue north through another gap between a ledge and a cliff, then head west towards some grass to battle Camper Sid who has a Lv 56 Dugtrio, a Lv 55 Primeape, and a Lv 56 Poliwrath. Jump the ledge to the south and head west to reach Cerulean City!

wt.title: Cerulean City
p: As you enter Cerulean City from Route 9 to the east, head west as you enter town to find the Pokécenter to the south. There aren't any NPC's in town with goodies to give, so let's follow up on that tip from the Power Plant guard, and head to the Gym to investigate.

wt.title: Machine Part
p: As you enter the gym, a Rocket Grunt will run into you. He'll ask you to forget him, and run off. Leave the gym and follow the white path east, north, and then west. Align yourself with the roof of the Pokécenter and head north to reach Route 24. You'll see the Rocket Grunt on the bridge you are on, talk to him to start a battle, he has a Lv 30 Koffing. Upon victory, he'll tell you that he hid the Machine Part in the Cerulean City gym. Fly back to Cerulean and enter the gym. You'll notice a flash on the floor just below the central pool of water. Interact with the tile that flashed to find the Machine Part. Our next objective is to return this part to the Power Plant!

wt.title: Power Plant Revisited/Zapdos
p:
Along with fixing the generator, we will also have the opportunity to catch Zapdos at the Power Plant, so be sure and heal up and stock up on Pokeballs if necessary! From Cerulean City, take the path east out of town towards Route 9. Jump a ledge to the south, walk to the square east of the trainer you see, and head east from there. Walk until you run into a cliff, then head north through a gap between a ledge and that cliff. Continue north through a gap between two ledges, head east, jump down a ledge to the south, and continue east to reach Route 10. Head north through a gap in the fence and surf east, south, and then disembark on the coast to the west to reach the Power Plant once again. 
 Enter the Power Plant and make your way to the opening in the wall towards the northeast corner of this room. Inside, speak to the Manager once more to return the Machine Part. You'll be given TM25 (Thunder) as a reward. Exit and then re-enter this room. Upon re-entry, you'll notice the worker guarding the exit to the west is no longer there. Take this exit to find a Lv 50 Zapdos!

wt.title: Route 24
p: From Cerulean City, take the bridge north out of town to reach Route 24. Continue north as far as you can. You'll notice a berry tree behind some ledges, it yields 10 Kelpsy Berries. Jump the ledge south of this tree, and head east to reach Route 25.

wt.title: Route 25
p:
Continue east as you enter Route 25 to battle School Kid Dudley, he has a Lv 56 Vileplume. The next trainer is Lass Ellen who has a Lv 55 Wigglytuff and a Lv 55 Granbull. Walk to the square just north Ellen and walk north one step, three steps east, and two steps south to battle School Kid Joe who has a Lv 56 Tangela and a Lv 56 Vaporeon. Walk one step west, two steps north, one step west, three steps north, and then four steps east to battle Lass Laura. Laura has a Lv 55 Bellossom, a Lv 55 Politoed, and a Lv 55 Pidgeot. 
 Walk south three steps, east two steps, and then interact with Camper Lloyd from behind, he has a Lv 57 Nidoking. Walk two steps west, three steps north, four steps east, and then three steps north to battle Lass Shannon. Shannon has a two Lv 56 Parasects, and a a Lv 55 Tangela. Walk south one step and head east. You'll see a berry tree which yields 10 Kelpsy Berries behind a cuttable tree. Just east is Super Nerd Pat who has a Lv 56 Porygon, a Lv 56 Magneton, and a Lv 56 Porygon2. Continue east to meet Cool Trainer Kevin who will award you with a Big Nugget for beating all the trainers, and then challenge you to a battle. Kevin has a Lv 58 Rhyhorn, a Lv 57 Lanturn, a Lv 58 Charizard, and a Lv 57 Espeon.
 Continue east, past a house to the north, to find a cliff with two NPCs on it. Approach the NPCs to cause one to run off, and the other to complain about your interruption. She will eventually reveal herself to be the Cerulean Gym Leader Misty, and tell you to come challenge her at here gym. Before we do this, head into the house we just walked by on this route.

wt.title: Bill's Grandpa
p:
Inside the house on Route 25 you'll meet Bill's grandpa. He will ask you to show him different Pokémon and will reward you for doing so. The first Pokémon he wants to see is Spinda, which can be found on Route 5. You'll be awarded an Everstone. The next Pokémon he wants to see is Roselia, which can be found on Route 16. You'll be awarded a Leaf Stone. The next Pokémon he wants to see is Lotad, which can be found in the Beach area of the Kanto Safari Zone. You'll be awarded a Deepseatooth. The next Pokémon he wants to see is Growlithe, which can be found on Route 36. You'll be awarded a Sun Stone. The final Pokémon he wants to see is Pichu, which can be found on Route 31. You'll be awarded a Deepseascale.
 That's it for here, Fly back to Cerulean and heal up, it's time to take of the Gym!

wt.title: Cerulean City Gym
p: As you enter the gym, head towards the trainer closest to you to the east to battle Swimmer Parker, he has two Lv 57 Seadras and a Lv 57 Gyarados. The trainer on the west side of this pool is Swimmer Diana who has a Lv 57 Golduck, a Lv 57 Cloyster, and a Lv 57 Corsola. Just below Misty to the north is Swimmer Briana, she has two Lv 58 Seakings and a Lv 58 Azumarill. The final battle is with Leader Misty, she has a Lv 62 Golduck, a Lv 62 Quagsire holding a Quick Claw, a Lv 61 Vaporeon holding Leftovers, a Lv 61 Milotic, a Lv 62 Lapras holding Nevermeltice, and a Lv 63 Starmie holding Mystic Water. You'll be awarded the Cascadebadge upon victory, as well as TM03 (Water Pulse).

wt.title: Route 25 Revisited/Suicune Encounter
p: After defeating Misty, we can finally finish up the Suicune arc! Take the bridge north of Cerulean City toward Route 24, head east towards Route 25, and make your way east through the small maze of trainers to get back to the cliff where you initially found Misty on her date. This time, you'll see Suicune on the cliff. As you approach from the south, Eusine will catch up and finally concede that you are the chosen trainer for Suicune. Interact with it to battle a Lv 50 Suicune.

wt.title: Route 5
p: From Cerulean, head south out of town to reach Route 5. You'll notice some ledges bridging the gap between two fences down the center of the route. Jump five ledges and enter the house. Talking to the old lady will net you a Cleanse Tag. That's it for this route!

wt.title: Route 8
p: From Saffron City, head out of town via the eastern gate to reach Route 8. You'll find Biker Dwayne to the east as you enter the route, he has a Lv 57 Koffing, a Lv 58 Koffing, a Lv 59 Koffing, and a Lv 60 Koffing. Head south to find Biker Harris who has a Lv 59 Flareon. Head east to battle Biker Zeke who has a Lv 58 Crobat and a Lv 56 Muk. Follow the dirt path north and then east to battle Super Nerd Sam who has a Porygon2. Continue east to find a berry tree which yields 10 Tamato Berries. Just south of this tree is Super Nerd Tom who has two Lv 56 Magnemites and a Lv 56 Steelix. From here, walk south back onto the dirt path, and follow it east to reach Lavender Town.

wt.title: Lavender Town Radio Tower/Radio Upgrade
p: After fixing the generator at the Power Plant, head to the Radio Tower just east of the Pokécenter in Lavender Town and enter. Speak to the old man NPC to be given the Radio Upgrade. With this, we can now awaken the Snorlax in Vermilion City, let's Fly there now!

wt.title: Vermilion City Revisited/Snorlax
p: From the Pokécenter in Vermilion, follow the street east, south at the first branch, south at the second branch, west at the third branch into a wall, north up some stairs, and then east to find Snorlax. After acquiring the Radio Upgrade, press A to awaken and battle a Lv 50 Snorlax holding Leftovers. The cave opening previously blocked by Snorlax is the entrance to Diglett's Cave, our next target.

wt.title: Diglett's Cave
p: After entering the cave from Vermilion City, you'll descend a ladder to reach the main tunnel. The path is a straight shot northwest to a ladder which you will ascend. In the next room, take the exit to the south to reach Route 2.

wt.title: Route 2
p: After exiting Diglett's Cave, head south and enter the house. Speaking to the NPC inside will net you a Nugget. Exit the house, Cut the tree to the south, and walk south through a gate. Continue south to find a Carbos. Even further south is a Nugget on the ground. Make your way back north all the way to the entrance to Diglett's Cave and Cut the tree to the west. Go north from here to reach Pewter City!

wt.title: Pewter City/Legendary Wing
p:
As you enter Pewter City from Route 2 to the south, walk north to find the Pokécenter. From the Pokécenter, head east, north at the fork in the road, continuing north at the next fork. Wondering around the third fork just ahead is a chubby NPC who can teach your Pokémon Rollout. 
 Head back south, this time heading east onto the street in front of the Mart, and then north up some stairs onto a small cliff occupied by an NPC who is an old man. Talk to him to receive either the Silver Wing or the Rainbow Wing, dependant on what legendary you chose to face earlier in Johto. If you have followed the walkthrough to this point, you will receive the Silver Wing, and the section revolviong around the Lugia encounter will be explained once we finish up in Pewter City. For those who already have Lugia, here is a link to the section of the walkthrough about the Tin Tower/Ho-oh.
 From the old man, head back down the stairs and to the street to the east. Head north up some stairs to find a berry tree which yields 10 Pomeg Berries.

wt.title: Pewter City Museum/Claw & Root Fossil
p:
Our next target will be the east wing of the Pewter City Museum to the north. From the Pokécenter, head east, north at the first fork, and continue north past the second and third forks as far as you can go. Head west and then north up some stairs in front of the museum. Rather than entering, head east and enter the small building you see connected to the museum. On a table you will see two fossils, interact with them to receive the Claw Fossil and the Root Fossil. The scientist at the southern desk can resurrect fossils.
 Exit this building and head into the main entrance of the museum. You'll see a hiker NPC on the north side of the first floor who is looking for Shards. You can trade a Red Shard for a Sun Stone, a Yellow Shard for a Deepseatooth, a Green Shard for a Leaf Stone, and a Blue Shard for a Deepseascale. That wraps up the valuables around Pewter, exit the museum, head down the stairs, and follow the street west, south, and then east to reach the entrance to Pewter City Gym.

wt.title: Pewter City Gym
p: This gym is about as straight forward as they come! Head north to battle Camper Jerry who has a Lv 60 Dugtrio, a lv 58 Sandslash, and a Lv 60 Donphan. Just ahead is Leader Brock, he has Lv 66 Golem holding a Quick Claw, a Lv 66 Aerodactyl holding a Hard Stone, a Lv 66 Kabutops holding a Scope Lens, a Lv 66 Omastar holding a Focus Band, a Lv 66 Relicanth holding a Hard Stone, and a Lv 66 Kleavor holding a Quick Claw. You'll be awarded the Boulderbadge upon victory, as well as TM26 (Earthquake).

wt.title: Whirl Islands/Lugia
p:
If you've been following the walkthrough up to this point, you've already battled Ho-oh and will be ready to take on this section once you acquire the SIlver Wing in Kanto. If instead you elected to pursue Lugia first, you can take on this section once you've acquired the Silver WIng and the Clear Bell, and have taken on the Kimono Girls after receiving your 8th badge.
 Ensure you are stocked up on Pokeballs (Love or Level Balls ftw), as well as some Escape Ropes, then Fly to Cianwood. From the Pokécenter, walk to the southeastern corner of the island and begin surfing southeast. Just past a Swimmer close to Cianwood, you'll see the Southwest entrance into the Whirl Islands. You'll have to surf along the southern portion of this island, before going north and traversing across a whirlpool to the west in order to reach the entrance. Inside, go north and then descend a ladder. Ascend that same ladder to return to the first floor and grab the Full Restore east of the ladder. Descend and then reascend once more to come back to the first floor, then head south, and Surf east across a small pond. You'll find a Guard Spec to the south. Head north and descend the ladder.
 On the next floor, take two steps east, begin surfing east until you hit a cliff, then surf north until you disembark onto land to the north. Take four steps north, ignore the stairs you see to the north, and beging walking east. After a short distance, you'll see the path branch to the south, follow it south until you find a Big Nugget. Return to the stars we previously ignored by heading north and then west. After ascending the stairs, you'll see a cave with a large opening. Before entering the cave, walk around to the backside to find a Carbos. Walk back around and enter the cave.
 In the next room, follow the path north and then east and descend the ladder. Head west across the next room to find another ladder which you will descend. Head east across the next room to find yet another ladder which you will descend. In the next room, walk to the northwest corner of the small island you are on and begin surfing east. Ignore the small patch of land in front of a stairset to the north, and instead disembark on land further east which has a large cave opening. Within this cave is Lugia. If you've gotten here before acquiring the Silver Wing and defeating the Kimono Girls in Ecruteak, a Tentacruel will block your path. Speaking to it three times will start an encounter with a Lv 100 Tentacruel. You cannot catch this Pokémon, and if you manage to knock it out, it will heal itself and continue to block the path into the cave until you have gotten the Silver Wing and defeated the Kimono Girls.
 Inside the cave, if you selected "Silver" when speaking to Baoba earlier in the game, the Kimono Girls will be here. There will be a cutscene where they will perform a dance to summon a Lv 50 Lugia. If you selected "Gold" the Lugia you find will be Lv 70. Once you've battled Lugia, we will get back to collecting the rest of the items within the Whirl Islands, so go ahead and head south to exit the cave.
 Back outside of Lugia's cave, walk five steps east and then surf east a short distance and disembark onto the land in front of a tall set of stairs. Ascend the stairs, head west, ascend another set of stairs, head east, and then ascend yet another set of stairs. Head east to find a PP Max. Return west and surf north, ascend a waterfall, then disembark onto land to the east to find a Full Restore. Surf west and ascend another waterfall to the north. Disembark on the land to the east and ascend the ladder you see to the north.
 On the next floor, follow the path to the northeast to find a ladder which you will ascend, leading to an Ultra Ball. Use an escape rope to avoid having to make your way back to the entrance, we will need to enter from one of the other islands to collect the remaining items.
 Fly back to Cianwood and head to the northern shore directly north of the Pokécenter. We will be aiming to enter the northwest Whirl Island. Surf north 3 spaces, then head east. Traverse the whirlpool you see to the northeast and enter the cave. Inside, head east and descend the ladder you see to the northeast.
 On the next floor, walk two spaces west, then head south. You'll descend the easternmost small staircase to the south, walk east three spaces, then ascend another small staircase. Start making your way south, eventually descending a ladder you find to the southeast. In this room you will find a Max Revive. Ascend the ladder to return to the previous floor. Head south from the ladder and then west to eventually find a Calcium. Make your way back east to the ladder we just descended, north, south down the small set of stairs, east, and north up another small set of stairs. Continue north towards the ladder we originally descended down to this flood, then head south down the set of stairs to the southeast of the ladder. Continue south into the cliff, then head north up the stairs just east of your position. Continue north into the cliff, then descend the stairs you see to the southeast. You'll find a Full Restore. Use an Escape Rope here, we only have two more items to find in the northeast Whirl Island!
 Back outside, surf towards the whirlpool you see to the east and traverse across it. Continue east to find another whirlpool which you will traverse, and enter the cave opening just northwest of the whirlpool. Inside, head east and jump the ledge and collect a Rare Candy. Descend the ladder southwest of your position. Surf west across the water to find the final item in the Whirl Islands, an Escape Rope. Go ahead and use that to return outside!

wt.title: Route 3
p:
Head east out of Pewter City to reach Route 3. The first trainer you will face is Youngster Jimmy, he has a Lv 59 Raticate and a Lv 59 Arbok. Head north through a gap between ledges into a cliff and then east to battle Youngster Warren who has a Lv 60 Fearow. Continue east, south through a gap between a ledge and a cliff, and then east to battle Firebreather Otis. Otis has two Lv 58 Magmars and a Lv 60 Weezing. 
 Continue east, head north through a gap between a ledge and a cliff, east, and jump a ledge to the south to find Firebreather Burt who has a Lv 60 Weezing and a Lv 60 Magcargo. Head east into some grass to find a berry tree which yields 10 Pomeg Berries. Head north through a gap between a ledge and a cliff to reach the western portion of Route 4.

wt.title: Route 4 West
p: As you enter Route 4 from Route 3 to the south, walk north to find a Pokécenter. Head west from the entrance to of the Pokécenter to find an Ultra Ball. Inside the Pokécenter is move tutor who can teach your Pokémon Swagger. There is nothing else to do on this route, be sure and heal up before entering Mt. Moon to the east, you'll have a battle as soon as you enter.

wt.title: Mt. Moon/Rival Battle 6
p: Immediately upon entering Mt. Moon from Route 4, you'll be challenged to a battle by your Rival. His potential teams are as follows:

After defeating Silver, our next objective is to head up to Mt. Moon Square, and area reachable by the two ladders within Mt. Moon proper itself. 
 Note: if you've played Gen 1 Pokémon games before, you'll notice as you explore that Mt. Moon has seemingly had some cave ins. There are two ladders surrounded by rocks that are unreachable, and a certain scientist has found himself in a rocky situation. 
 The quickest way to reach Mt. Moon Square from the entrance is to head east into a cliff, three steps south, east past a small sign to the north, and then north at the first branch in the path. Ascend the ladder ahead to reach the Square.

wt.title: Mt. Moon Square/Jirachi
p:
After entering Mt. Moon Square, head east to find a house. Inside is a vendor who sells Moon Stones. The other NPC tells you that at night time, Clefairy come out to play, clueing you in to your next move. If it isn't already night time, adjust the time using the clock inside this house. Exit, jump the ledge to the south, take three steps south, and the head east into a rock. You'll find a Moon Stone to the south. 
 From here, head north through a gap in the fence. Assuming it is night time, you will see a group of Clefairies playing around a small pond. Make your way north to find an unusual white rock. Select "Yes" when prompted to touch the rock which causes Jirachi to appear! Interact with it start the encounter, it will be Lv 50.
 Once you finish the enocunter with Jirachi, it will be time to make our way to the exit of Mt. Moon. Make your way out of the fenced area, and head east until you run into a cliff. You'll enter the mouth in the cave you see to the southeast, which takes you back into Mt. Moon proper. 
 From the ladder you just descended, head east, north up some steps, east into a cliff, south into another cliff, east into a third cliff, and then south into the wall below. You'll ascend the staircase you see to the east which leads to the exit out of Mt. Moon!

wt.title: Route 4 East
p: As you enter Route 4 from Mt. Moon to the west, head east to see a berry tree which yields 10 Tamato Berries. Next to this tree is a move tutor who can teach your Pokémon Dynamicpunch. Jump a ledge to the east of this tutor and head south to battle Bird Keeper Hank, he has a Lv 59 Murkrow, and a Lv 59 Pidgeot. Jump another ledge to the south to battle Picnicker Sharon, she has a Lv 61 Furret, and a Lv 58 Rapidash. Head north through a gap between ledges, east, north through a gap between a ledge and some trees, and north through one more gap between ledges to battle Picnicker Hope who has a Lv 61 Ampharos. You'll find an Hp Up to the east between two ledges. That completes Route 4!

wt.title: Viridian Forest
p:
From Pewter City, head south out of town towards Route 2. Before heading through the gate to the south, Cut the tree you see blocking the path between two fences, and head into Diglett's Cave to the east. Assuming you've beaten him, you'll find Leader Brock inside. Talk to him to send him to the Fighting Dojo in Saffron for a rematch!
 Go back through the fence to Route 2 and then walk through the gate to the south. You'll find yourself in Viridian Forest. Head south to find Bug Catcher Doug who has a Lv 62 Ariados. Continue south into the treeline and the head east to find an Elixer. Head back to the dirt path to the west and go north through some grass and up some stairs to battle Bug Catcher Ed, he has three Lv 60 Beedrills. 
 Go east, south down some stairs, continue south through the grass, and then head east once you reach the dirt path. At the end of this path, head south into some grass until you reach the cliff's edge, and the go east to find Leader Bugsy. Speak to him to transport him to the Fighting Dojo in Saffron where you can challenge him to a rematch. Just west of where Bugsy was is a Full Restore.
 Head back east and continue north until you ascend some stairs to find a Revive. Head north until you hit the treeline, go east, and then south down some stairs and into the treeline. Go west until you reach the dirt path, follow that path south down some stairs, and go east to find a Dire Hit. 
 Head back to the dirt path to the west, south through some grass until you hit the treeline, and then west until you find a Full Heal in a patch of grass in the southwest corner of the forest. Go east out of this patch of grass, north at the first fork until you hit a cliff, and then west to find a Max Ether. Take one step south before heading east to find a Max Potion. Head south from here, around a large tree, and take the exit out of Viridian Forest!

wt.title: Viridian City
p: After exiting the gate from Viridian Forest to the north, head south through a small portion of Route 2 to reach Viridian City! The Pokécenter is in the southern portion of the town. From the entrance of the Pokécenter, head west and Surf across a small pond to find a move tutor who can teach your Pokémon Sleep Talk. Just northeast of the Pokécenter is the Mart. Inside of the mart is a move tutor who can teach your Pokémon Double-Edge. The gym leader is currently gone from his gym, we won't be able to challenge him until we get our 15th badge.

wt.title: Contest Hall
p: The building directly north of the Viridian City Pokécenter is the Contest Hall. I will update this section once I've had the chance to reacclimate myself with Contest mechanics, for now, I would suggest Googling "gen 3 Pokémon contests mechanics" if you're wanting to take them on.

wt.title: Route 1
p: Go south from the Pokécenter in Viridian City to reach Route 1. Just as you enter the route, head west between two trees to find a berry tree which yields 5 Sitrus Berries. Head east to get back on the dirt path, then jump a ledge into a patch of grass to the south. In this grass is Cool Trainer Quinn who has a Lv 58 Ivysaur and a Lv 58 Starmie. Continue south, following the dirt path until you meet School Kid Danny. Danny has a Lv 55 Jynx, a Lv 55 Magmar, and a Lv 55 Electabuzz. Pallet Town is just south of where Danny is!

wt.title: Pallet Town
p: Welcome to Pallet Town! There is only one thing to do here, and that won't become available until we have all 16 badges. Let's head to the water on the south side of town and Surf to continue our journey.

wt.title: Route 21
p: From Pallet Town, start surfing south to enter Route 21. As you surf south, you'll see a lone NPC on an island to the east. This is Fisherman Arnold, he has a Lv 61 Lanturn and a Lv 61 Quagsire. Continue surfing south, the next trainer you will battle is Swimmer Seth who has a Lv 59 Quagsire, a Lv 59 Octillery, and a Lv 59 Gyarados. Continue surfing south past three islands to battle Swimmer Nikki. She has two Lv 58 Dewgongs and a Lv 58 Cloyster. Continue surfing south to reach Cinnabar Island! You can disembark on the southern side of the island.

wt.title: Cinnabar Island
p: Welcome to Cinnabar Island! There isn't a whole lot left on the island itself due to a volcanic explosion. Inside the Pokécenter, the NPC with the blonde hair is a move tutor who can teach your Pokémon Explosion. Outside, you can find Blue, the gym leader of Viridian City, hanging out in front of a pond to the north of the Pokécenter. To get him to return to Viridian City for a gym battle, we must collect 15 badges and then talk to him here. Where is the Cinnabar Island Gym you might ask? Let's heal up at the Pokécenter, and continue our expedition east.

wt.title: Route 20 West
p: From the Pokécenter on Cinnabar Island, walk to the shoreline to the south and surf east as far as you can, north as far as you can, and then continue east to reach Route 20. Just as you enter the route, you'll see a Fisherman and his golden Magikarp named Dennis. Best not to antagonize that particular fish, I've seen it Splash legendaries to death firsthand! Swimming east of Dennis Island is Swimmer Lori who has two Lv 62 Starmies. Continue east to find the west entrance to the Seafoam Islands.

wt.title: Cinnabar Gym (Seafoam Islands)
p: As you enter the western entrance to the Seafoam Islands from Route 20, descend the ladder you see to the north to find the hidden Cinnabar Gym. The only trainer here is Leader Blaine. Blaine has a Lv 66 Rapidash holding a Quick Claw, a Lv 65 Magmortar holding a Sitrus Berry, a Lv 66 Houndoom holding a Miracle Seed, a Lv 65 Magcargo holding Leftovers, a Lv 67 Torkoal holding a White Herb, and a Lv 67 Camerupt holding Charcoal. Victory will net you the Volcanobadge and TM50 (Overheat).

wt.title: Seafoam Islands/Articuno
p: As you enter the southern entrance to the Seafoam Islands from Route 20 to the west, walk west, south down a large set of stairs, south down a small set of stairs, seven steps west, and thirteen steps north. We have to bike across some broken ice here, so mount your bike and press R to switch gears.

Cross the three cracked ice tiles to the west and stop. From the now exposed hole in the ice, take three steps west to align yourself with a cracked ice tile to the north. Mount your bike, press R to shift gears, and bike north across the ice, some solid ground, and then eventually into some rocks above two rows of cracked ice, which you will fall through.

Falling through the ice will land you in some water. Surf north to find Articuno; it will be Lv 50. To exit the cave from here, ascend the stairs west of Articuno. Jump the ledge south of the ladder to skate across a large patch of ice. Continue south into a rock, then take a step east to fall through cracked ice. Walk south, surf south across some water onto land, take four steps south, walk east until you reach some water, and surf south until you disembark onto land. Walk west, north up some stairs, and ascend the ladder. 
 Walk south down a small set of stairs, east, north up a small set of stairs, and then north up a large set of stairs. The exit is to the east of the top of the large set of stairs!

wt.title: Cinnabar Island Revisited/Blue
p: Once you have 15 badges, Fly to Cinnabar and speak to the NPC standing in the center of the island. This is the Viridian City gym leader, Blue, and he will head back to Viridian where we can now challenge him and get our final badge.

wt.title: Route 19/Route 20 East
p:
From the Fuchsia City Pokécenter, head south out of town to Route 19 and begin surfing south. Shortly after entering the water, you will battle Swimmer Jerome. He has a Lv 58 Vaporeon, a Lv 58 Tentacruel, and a Lv 58 Seaking. Surf 5-6 spaces west before continuing to surf south. You'll see two NPCs side by side in the water. The NPC on the left is Swimmer Tucker who has a Lv 60 Quilfish and a Lv 60 Cloyster. The NPC on the right is Swimmer Dawn who has a Lv 60 Seaking. Surf 8-9 spaces east before continuing south to battle Swimmer Harold, he has a Lv 62 Octillery and a Lv 61 Seadra. Below Harold is a cave that will be blocked off until you beat the Kanto League. Surf west from the cave to reach the eastern portion of Route 20.
 Continue surfing west on Route 20 to find Swimmer Cameron on the southern portion of this route. Cameron has a Lv 64 Azumarill. Continue surfing west and then north to battle Swimmer Nicole who has a Lv 60 Mantine, and a Lv 63 Lapras. Disembark onto the shore and continue west, you'll find a Shell Bell on the beach close to the northern entrance to Seafoam Islands. That is it for these routes, Fly to Viridian City and heal up, it's time to get our final badge!

wt.title: Viridian City Gym
p: From the Pokécenter in Viridian, head to the gym in the northeast portion of town. Assuming you have collected 15 badges and spoken to Leader Blue on Cinnabar, he will be awaiting you as the sole trainer in his gym. Blue has a Lv 69 Rhyperior holding a Sitrus Berry, a Lv 68 Pidgeot holding a Sharp Beak, a Lv 67 Machamp holding a Scope Lens, a Lv 68 Exeggutor holding Leftovers, a Lv 68 Tyranitar holding a Focus Band, and a Lv 69 Arcanine holding a Silk Scarf. Upon victory you'll be awarded the Earthbadge and TM08 (Bulk Up).

wt.title: Pallet Town/Oak Unlocking Mt. Silver
p: After acquiring your sixteenth badge, Fly to Pallet Town and head into Oak's Laboratory. Speaking to Oak will result in him lauding you for collecting all the badges in Kanto and will unlock Mt. Silver. We won't head there quite yet, but it is reachable via the gate leading to Victory Road.

wt.title: Route 22/Celebi Cutscene
p:
Route 22 is a small route west of Viridian which leads to the gate connecting Johto to Kanto right before Victory Road. There is an optional cutscene available to those who have caught Celebi, if you have, make sure Celebi is at the head of your party before heading to Route 22. From the Viridian City Pokécenter, head west, north at the bend in the road, west at the first branch in the road, and then continue west to reach Route 22. 
 Jump the ledge to the south and follow the brick road west. As you pass the fourth streetlamp, Celebi will suddenly jump and transport you back in time where you will discover the parentage and true motive of your Rival. There is one more event unlocked by Celebi, so let's check that out before taking on the Kanto League!

wt.title: Tohjo Falls/Celebi Cutscene/Giovanni Battle
p:
Be sure Celebi is in your party and heal your party, we have a battle coming up. Remember that old radio in Tohjo Falls? It's time to head back and find out what that was. Fly to New Bark Town and Surf east out of town onto Route 27 and enter the cave opening into Tohjo Falls. Climb the waterfall, surf east, descend another waterfall, and then disembark onto the land to the west. After walking west a short distance, you'll see a cave opening to the north. 
 Put Celebi at the head of your party and enter the cave. After taking a step inside, Celebi will jump and transport you back in time where you will witness Giovanni hearing the Rocket broadcast from the radio tower alerting him to their return to power. He will inform you of his intent to rejoin his team at Goldenrod and will challenge you to a battle. Rocket Admin Giovanni has a Lv 60 Kangaskhan holding Leftovers, a Lv 61 Persian, a Lv 61 Honchkrow, a Lv 61 Nidoqueen, a Lv 60 Ursaluna, and a Lv 62 Nidoking. Getting beat by a child once more causes Giovanni to ditch his dreams for good!

wt.title: Indigo Plateau/Rival Battle 7
p: Assuming you have acquired all 16 badges, it is now time to take on the Kanto Elite 4! Fly to Indigo Plateau and heal up. You'll see your Rival in front of the entrance leading to the Elite 4, he will challenge you one final time. His potential parties are:

wt.title: Kanto Elite 4
p:
Heal up once more after defeating your Rival and then enter the room leading to the E4.
 Your first battle will be against the Psychic user, Elite 4 Will.
In the next room you'll battle the Poison specialist, Elite 4 Koga.
In the third room, the Fighting user Elite 4 Bruno will be your opponent.
In the next room you'll battle the final member of the Elite 4, the Dark loving Elite 4 Karen.
In the final room, you'll be taking on the Dragon master, Champion Lance.

Upon victory, your party will be once again entered into the Hall Of Fame. You'll in New Bark Town after the credits roll. Any legendaries and static encounters (like Sudowoodo) will now respawn, and will continue to respawn upon each subsequent defeat of the Kanto E4 going forward. The GS Ball will also respawn at it's location in the Ruins of Alph, it has the second best catch odds of any ball in game, so be sure and snag that!

wt.title: Kanto Safari Zone Steven/Eon Ticket
p: After you've beaten the Kanto E4, Fly to Fuchsia and head to the Safari Zone to the north. Speak to Steven (the NPC with gray hair at a table) to receive the Eon Ticket! We will be using this shortly.

wt.title: South Olivine City/Auroraticket
p: Fly to Olivine City. From the Pokécenter, walk south as far as you can, and then walk eleven steps east. Assuming you've beaten the Kanto E4, talking to the NPC standing under the canopy will net you the Auroraticket! We will be using this shortly.

wt.title: Southern Island/Latias & Latios
p: Once you have acquired the Eon Ticket from Steven, Fly to Olivine. From the Pokécenter, head south into the pier where the SS Aqua is docked. Speak to the Sailor and select Southern Island. There is only one path, follow it to enter a forest area to the north. Here you will find two Pokémon. The red one is a Lv 50 Latias, the blue is a Lv 50 Latios. After battling both, return to the Sailor and speak to him to head back to Olivine.

wt.title: Birth Island/Deoxys
p:
Once you have acquired the Auroraticket from the NPC in Olivine, head south into the pier where the SS Aqua is docked. Speak to the Sailor and select Birth Island. This is a small island featuring four meteorites scattered around, and a triangle in the center. Interacting with the triangle will cause it to move. To summon the legendary here, you must take the shortest path to the triangle and interact with it after it moves. To start, interact with the southern face. Take one step south, three steps west, then interact with the eastern face. Take three steps east, five steps north, then interact with the southern face. Take five steps south, three steps east, then interact with the western face. Take three steps north, five steps west, then interact with the eastern face. Take four steps east then interact with the western face. Take two steps west, two steps south, then interact with the northern face. Take one step south, three steps west, then interact with the eastern face. Take six steps east and interact with the western face. Take three steps west and interact with the northern face. Finally, take three steps north then interact with the southern face to summon a Lv 70 Deoxys. 
 Note: Unlike most stationary Pokémon, Deoxys will flee if you run away, so be sure and save before interacting with the triangle the final time if you'd like to shiny hunt Deoxys. Soft resetting is necessary to accomplish this feat.
 If you have Deoxys in your party and return to Birth Island, you can interact with the meteorites to change it's form. Each form affects the stats and the Ability of Deoxys. The northern meteorite draws out the Speed Form, the western meteorite draws out the Attack Form, the meteorite in the eastern corner draws out the Normal Form, and the meteorite just north of the one in the eastern corner draws out the Defense Form. You can change Deoxys' form as often as you'd like!

wt.title: Route 47 Revisited/Embedded Tower/Rayquaza
p:
Once you've beaten the Kanto League, Rayquaza is now available to catch. Fly to the Safari Zone Gate. From there, head south across a bridge, east across a bridge, south past a berry tree and down a small set of stairs, west across a bridge, south, east across a bridge, north, east across a bridge, and north into a cave. 
 Descend the ladder, descend another ladder, then south out of the cave. Surf south as far as you can, head west past a beach occupied by a Staryu, then disembark on a beach with a tall staircase. Head north up two staircases then enter the cave entrance into the Embedded Tower. Inside you can encounter a Lv 70 Rayquaza.

wt.title: Route 19 Revisited/Kyogre
p: Once you've beaten the Kanto League, Kyogre is now available to catch. Fly to Fuchsia City and head south out of town towards Route 19. Surf south as far as you can and disembark on the bank of a cave on the southeast corner of the route. Inside this cave is a Lv 70 Kyogre.

wt.title: Seafoam Islands Revisited/Groudon
p: Once you've beaten the Kanto League, Groudon is now available to catch. Fly to Cinnabar Island and surf east towards Route 20. Continue surfing east until you reach the southern entrance to the Seafoam Islands. Enter the cave and descend the ladder into Blaine's Gym. Behind the platform where Blaine previously stood is a cave entrance. In here, you'll find a Lv 70 Groudon.

wt.title: Cerulean Cave/Mewtwo
p:
Once you have beaten the Kanto League, Cerulean Cave will be open. Fly to Cerulean and head north out of town towards Route 24. After crossing the bridge, surf south on the water west of the bridge until you can disembark on land in front of a cave opening. This is the entrance to Cerulean Cave.
 After entering the cave, smash a rock and surf north, disembarking on the land just north of the entrance with a ladder you can ascend. Ascend the ladder and follow the path, smashing two rocks along the way, to find a Protein. 
 Return to and descend the ladder back to the first floor and begin surfing west. Once you get to a branch in the path, disembark onto the land to the north. The ladder you see to the north leads nowhere, so head west and collect the PP Up on the ground. Head south from where you just found the PP Up and ascend the ladder you see just north of a smashable rock. Once again, follow the path, smashing one rock along the way, to find a Zinc. 
 Return to and descend the ladder back to the first floor. Head south from the ladder, smash the rock, and collect the Rare Candy on the ground. Smash another rock in front of a small staircase to the east, head up the stairs onto a cliff, and head east as far as you can. Head north to find a Max Elixer just east of a ladder. Ascend that ladder and follow the short path south, smashing a rock along the way, to find a Big Pearl.
 Return to and descend the ladder back to the first floor. Head west, smash a rock in front of a small set of stairs to the south, and ascend the ladder you see on a small cliff to the east. This path isn't as straightforward as the others we have encountered in this cave to this point. Head west, then turn south at the first branch in the path. Proceed west, then south two steps, east four steps, and follow this path south, east, north, and then east until you reach a ladder, which you will descend.
 Descend one more ladder on the next floor then head north, east, then smash a rock in front of a small set of stairs. Head east, north, then east and smash a rock. Hugging the wall to the north, proceed east until you can go north between two cliffs to find an Ultra Ball. Walk south as far as you can, then west and smash a rock in front of a small set of stairs. Ascend the small set of stairs, take two steps east, then head north to find a Max Revive. Head west and smash a rock in front a small set of stairs to the south. Follow this path south until you come across another rock blocking a set of stairs, smash that rock and ascend the stairs. Surf ten spaces west on the water you see to the west, surf north, and disembark onto a small cliff where you can encounter a Lv 80 Mewtwo!

wt.title: Gym Leader Rematches Summary
p: As previously discussed, you can find the gym leaders at various places in the overworld after defeating them. Speaking to them will cause them to transport to the Fighting Dojo in Saffron City where you can challenge them to rematches which net 10 BP upon defeat. Most of them can be found as soon as you defeat the Johto League, though there are a couple of exceptions that will be noted below. If you've followed the walkthrough to this point, there are a handful that we have already encountered. This section will consolidate that information so one can use this section to find everyone.
Falkner: Falkner is found on the fifth floor of the Celadon Department Store.

wt.title: Bugsy: Bugsy is found in Viridian Forest.
Whitney: Whitney is found on the sixth floor of the Goldenrod Department Store.
Morty: Morty is found in front of this house on the southeast corner of Bellchime Trail which leads to the Tin Tower.
Chuck: Chuck is apparently still "training" in his gym.
Jasmine: Jasmine is found inside the Olivine Cafe, the building just west of the Pokécenter.
p: Pryce: Pryce is found on the southwest side of the Lake of Rage.

wt.title: Claire: Claire is found in the Dragon's Den.
p: Brock: Brock is found inside the entrance to Diglett's Cave, accessible from Route 2.
Misty: Misty is found just south of the Sea Cottage on Route 25.
LT Surge: LT Surge is found in front of the Power Plant.
Erika: Erika is found just south of the Celadon Department Store.
Janine: Janine is found in the gate leading to Victory Road. The quickest way to get here is through Route 22.
Sabrina: Sabrina is found on the Olivine Docks.
Blaine: Blaine is found on Cinnabar Island after acquiring your sixteenth badge.
Blue: Blue is found in his gym after acquiring his badge. Exit and reenter the gym after defeating him to trigger the new dialogue.

Here are the teams used by the Gym Leaders for their rematches! The Johto leaders will have new teams, the Kanto ones will retain the teams they originally had. You can challenge them however many times you'd like.

wt.title: Route 28
p:
Once you've acquired all sixteen badges and then spoken to Oak, the path to Mt. Silver will be unlocked. Head west out of Viridian City to Route 22. On the western side of this route is the gate that leads to Victory Road. As you enter the gate, walk across the center hallway to the hallway going west and exit.
 You'll now be on Route 28! Take one step west, then walk south into a cliff. Take twelve steps west, surf across the small pond into grass to the south, walk west until you hit a tree, one step north, west into a cliff, south, and then north up a small staircase. Walk west until you see another staircase to the north, head north up the stairs, and then west until you see yet another staircase. Walk north up these stairs, and follow the dirt path north and then west until you come to a Pokécenter.
 From the entrance of the Pokécenter, walk east into the grass next to the Pokécenter, north into a cliff, then east until you see a staircase. Head south down these stairs, east, and south down another set of stairs. Head east on the path while hugging the trees to the north until you hit a cliff, north, until you see a set of stairs, then head south down these stairs. Walk east and enter the house you see to the north. Speak to the NPC in this house to receive TM47 (Steel Wing). From here, either walk back or Fly to the Pokécenter outside of Mt. Silver.

wt.title: Mt. Silver/Moltres
p:
From the entrance of the Pokécenter, jump the ledge to the east and head north to find a cave opening into Mt. Silver. After entering the mountain, walk west and begin surfing. Surf two spaces west and then north up a waterfall. Dismbark onto a staircase to the north and enter the cave opening you see. Inside this cave is a Spell Tag.
 Exit the cave, surf west, and disembark on the bank to the west. Head up the small staircase and walk west to find an Ultra Ball. Return to the water and surf north, disembarking onto the tall staircase you see. You'll find a Full Restore on the ground to the west. Head back east to the small staircase slightly north, surf north up a waterfall, disembark onto a staircase to the north, then enter the cave opening you see. 
 Walk west into a cliff, north, east at the first branch in the path, and then south down a large set of stairs. You'll encounter a Lv 50 Moltres here. After your encounter with Moltres, either walk back to the entrance of Mt Silver, or use an Escape Rope.

wt.title: Mt. Silver/Red
p:
Back at the entrance of Mt. Silver, walk north up a large staircase to find a Max Potion. Walk through the cave opening you see to the east. Outside, walk east into the cliffside, south, north up a set of stairs, west, north up another set of stairs, west, and north up yet another set of stairs. Continue north, south down a set of stairs to the east, six steps south, and enter the cave opening to the west. Inside this cave you will find a Dire Hit.
 Exit the cave and go south down a set of stairs to the east. Walk east, south down a set of stairs, and make your way to another set of stairs to the south. Go north up these stairs and walk west into a cave opening to the west.
 Once inside, walk west until you can head north, continuing north up a large set of stairs and into a cave opening to the north. In the next room, walk north up a set of stairs, west into a cliff, north up another set of stairs, west into the wall, south until you hit another wall, east, north at the branch in the path and up a set of stairs to the north. Walk west into a cliff, north up a set of stairs, and then east until you see a cave opening to the north.
 You'll arrive back outside in a snowy portion of Mt. Silver. Walk east as far as you can and then south, ignoring the first cave opening you see to the west. Continue south and enter the second cave opening you see to the west. Inside, walk south and exit a cave opening you see to the east.
 Back outside, walk south as far as you can, west past a cave opening to the north, north up a set of stairs you see just west of the cave opening, west, north up a second set of stairs, east, and then north to find a Nevermeltice. Head back south down the two sets of stairs we just climbed and then enter the cave opening just east of the second set of stairs. Head west and then south through a cave opening to the south. Back outside, head north up a set of stairs to the east of the cave opening, then west. Head north up the westernmost staircase, continuing north up a second staircase to find a Rare Candy. Head back south down the two sets of stairs, and then head north up the set of stairs just east of the second set of stairs. Continue north up another set of stairs and enter the cave opening to the north.
 Inside, head west, north up a large set of stairs, and enter the cave opening to the north. On the summit, you will find PKMN Trainer Red to the north. Prepare yourself for the most difficult battle in the main storyline of the game! Red's team is:

After defeating Red, the credits will roll, and you will reawaken in New Bark Town. Congratulations, assuming you've followed the walkthrough, you've beaten the main storyline of the game! If you haven't completed your Pokedex, now would be a great time to do so. Remember, once you've completed your dex, you can talk to the Game Designer inside Celadon Mansion to receive your Diploma. 

 After completing your dex, the Battle Frontier will likely hold the final content for you to exhaust! I'd recommend starting a new run and playing around with the randomizer settings for a completely unique run, even after several playthroughs during my playtesting, the randomizer was a gamechanger for this Pokémon Trainer. There are currently a bunch of ways for you to change up the core experience. Also, stay tuned, our wonderful devs have even more new features in store for the eventual release of V2.0. Thanks a ton for following along, I hope this walkthrough proved to be a valuable resource!
 --headlocker03

table: Pokemon
How do I get [Pokemon] from the Odd Egg?
The bookshelves in the day care contain the answer combinations for each Pokemon. Read them left to right.
Note: The Odd Egg has a 14% chance to hatch a Shiny Pokemon.
Shiny
How do I hunt a shiny starter?
Save before interacting with any of the three balls. Interact with a ball, and if the starter is shiny, the picture of the Pokemon that appears will be shiny too.
Technical
How do I download and patch the game?
See download or Hackdex: https://www.hackdex.app/hack/pokemon-heart-and-soul
Gameplay
How do I enter the Ruins of Alph puzzle chambers?
This is different from the vanilla games; it requires using the Pokemon for the respective puzzle. Make sure they're in the front slot of your party.
(For fossil Pokemon) Solve the puzzle room and collect the fossil when it appears.
Shiny
How do I get Shiny Pokemon? Is [Pokemon] shiny locked?

Check Gifts & Statics for shiny locks. For gift Pokemon, save the game (not a save state) and soft reset. For overworld interact encounters - excluding Mew, Deoxys and the first Celebi - run away and re-encounter. For wild Pokemon in grass, caves or water, just keep encountering.
Items
How do I get Nature Mints?
They are available in the Goldenrod Flower Shop after defeating Whitney.
Items
How do I get special Pokeballs?

Bring Kurt berries in Azalea Town. His balls keep their Heart & Soul 1.2 type-based behaviour as well as their GSC and HGSS behaviour. They are the only Pokeballs in the game besides the regular, Great, Ultra, Master and Premier balls.
Berry and ball details are on Items & TMs .
Items
Where are the plates in Sinjoh?

All 17 plates are found in Sinjoh. The numbers match the map in the detailed answer, and each plate links to its exact location on Items & TMs : 1. Fist Plate 2. Toxic Plate 3. Sky Plate 4. Mind Plate 5. Dread Plate 6. Splash Plate 7. Flame Plate 8. Earth Plate 9. Spooky Plate 10. Meadow Plate 11. Icicle Plate 12. Pixie Plate 13. Draco Plate 14. Insect Plate 15. Iron Plate 16. Zap Plate 17. Stone Plate
Click the map for the full-size version.
Other
Can I save state reset for shinies, natures or EVs?

Technically yes, but in practice no. You reload the same seed every time, so encountering at the same moment hits the same few frames over and over. You would have to vary your actions slightly, which is slower. Soft resetting is easier and more effective.
Other
Is broken Emerald RNG fixed?
Yes, it is fixed in this game, and soft resetting changes your seed.
Pokemon
How does [Pokemon] evolve?
Check the Evolution tab for that species on Pokédex . Methods differ from the vanilla games in places.
Pokemon
How do I find legendary Pokemon?
Check Gifts & Statics for locations, and Items & TMs for the key items some of them need.
Pokemon
How do I switch a Pokemon's ability?
Use an Ability Capsule, available at the Saffron Dojo and the Battle Frontier.

Hidden abilities do exist in this game - a species' hidden ability is listed on its card on Pokédex . Some legendaries also get a different ability when the LEGEN. ABILITIES setting is on; that is shown on their card too.
Pokemon
How do trade evolutions work?
You can still trade locally for them. You can also level them up while holding the item that would normally be involved in the trade.
Pokemon
Are Gen IV and later evolutions available?

Yes, many are. Anything that evolves from a Generation 1-3 family is in - Magnezone, Rhyperior, Electivire, Magmortar, Togekiss, Leafeon, Glaceon, Sylveon, Gliscor, Mamoswine, Porygon-Z, Weavile and more.
Check the Evolution tab on a species in Pokédex for its exact method.
Time
When are the time of day cutoffs?
Day (for encounters, overworld Pokemon and evolutions): 6am-6:59pm Night (for encounters, overworld Pokemon and evolutions): 7pm-5:59am
Story
What's up with the radio in Tohjo Falls? How do I battle Giovanni? Where is the HGSS Giovanni/Silver scene?
Put Celebi first in your party and enter the Tohjo Falls radio room to trigger the Giovanni battle. Put Celebi first and explore Route 22 to trigger the Giovanni/Silver scene.
Items
What are the best ways to make money?
A few that work at different points in the game:

Bug Contest first prize only needs a Pinsir or Scyther, and the evolution stone reward sells for 5,000. Get a Butterfree or Venonat with Compound Eyes and hunt for held items - Grimer for Nuggets, Magnemite for Metal Coats, Slowpoke for King's Rocks. Compound Eyes gives a 20% held-item chance. Nuggets and King's Rocks sell for 5,000; Metal Coats and Moon Stones sell for 1,500. Sell Kurt's berry balls - they are easy to farm in bulk. The Amulet Coin is in the Goldenrod Department Store basement, and works as long as anyone in your party is holding it.
Time
Can I change the time of day?
Change the clock from the Pokemon Center. This may lock you out of certain daily events for 24 hours.
Difficulty
What happens to level caps after badge 8?
With the level cap setting on, the caps after badge 8 are based on Johto Champion Lance's party, then Kanto Champion Lance's party.
Nuzlocke, Randomizer
Why is my Pokemon able to use X move from the party menu?
In certain nuzlocke and randomizer configurations, the first party Pokemon can use more field moves to prevent softlocks.
Nuzlocke
Why can I catch infinite Pokemon in the Bug Contest or Safari Zone?
The Bug Contest and Safari Zone have specific items and quests built around catching Pokemon, so nuzlocke rules are disabled in those locations.
Randomizer
Why won't the move relearner help me?
Due to technical limitations, move relearning is disabled when random moves is turned on.
Story
How do I get to Mt. Silver?
Talk to Oak after 16 badges.
Gameplay
Why can't I see my Pokemon's head when I walk in front of a lamp?
GBA limitation. It was either no glows, or glows with a few compromises.
Story
I can't get past the RageCandyBar guy in Mahogany Town.
After beating Pryce, Elm calls to say Rockets have taken over the Goldenrod Radio Tower. Go to Goldenrod and deal with it. You also need 7 badges in total, so make sure Chuck and Jasmine are beaten.
Story
How do I fix the Power Plant?
Talk to the chief engineer at the Power Plant. As you go to leave, a guard asks for help.

Go to Misty's gym and you'll run into a Rocket grunt. Find that grunt again on Nugget Bridge, battle and beat him. Return to the gym - the camera zooms in on a sparkle. Interact with the spot that sparkled to get the Machine Part.
Story
How do I get past the Kinglers south of Fuchsia City?
They clear once you have progressed far enough through Kanto. You need at least Lt. Surge's badge to begin.

Surf to the Power Plant east of Cerulean to start the Machine Part quest. Go to Cerulean Gym to run into the Rocket grunt and recover the Machine Part. Return the Machine Part to the Power Plant. Get the Expansion Card from the Director at the Lavender Town Radio Tower. Wake the Snorlax east of Vermilion and go through Diglett's Tunnel to Pewter City. Travel down through Pallet Town to Cinnabar Island. Work through the Cinnabar storyline and Seafoam Islands. The Kinglers will be gone.
Story
How do I get to Lugia or Ho-Oh?
You need the Silver Wing (Lugia) or Rainbow Wing (Ho-Oh), all 8 Johto badges, the Master Ball from Prof. Elm, and to have defeated the Kimono Girls in Ecruteak City afterwards.
Gameplay
Why can't I open this door?
It's just there to look nice. Don't worry, we tried it a bunch too.
Gameplay
How do I rematch the gym leaders?
Every gym leader you have met can be rematched. Each one waits in a specific place, and the conditions differ between Johto and Kanto leaders.
See Trainers - each leader's card lists their rematch location and when it unlocks on the rematch battle's tab.
Pokemon
Can you complete the Pokedex in this game?
Yes. Every Pokemon in the Pokedex can be caught, obtained or evolved.
See Pokédex for every species, and Completion for what completion requires.
Pokemon
What Pokemon are in this romhack? What legendaries and mythicals can I find?

Heart & Soul began as a GBA remake of Crystal built on Emerald, so the roster is built from Generation 1-3 families. Later-generation Pokemon appear only where they are an evolution of one of those families - Magnezone, Togekiss, Sylveon, Mamoswine and Weavile are all in, for example.
See Pokédex for the full list, and Wild Encounters for where each one lives.
Pokemon
Is [Regional Form] Pokemon in the game?
There are no regional forms available.
Pokemon
Can we change the IVs or EVs of our Pokemon?
IVs cannot be changed. EVs can be reduced with the EV-lowering berries available in Kanto.
Berry locations are listed on Items & TMs .
Pokemon
Can you get Larvitar in Dark Cave before Falkner?
Yes. Larvitar appears on the Dark Cave South Side - the part reachable from the start - during the day, at a 5% encounter rate, at levels 2-4.
Full encounter tables are on Wild Encounters .
Shiny
What's the best way to shiny hunt Entei and Raikou?

Entei and Raikou roam independently - both start roaming as soon as you awaken them in the Burned Tower, and neither gates the other. Their shininess and IVs are decided when they are created, so the way to re-roll them is to have them created again by beating the Kanto League.

Both are created together at level 40 by the Burned Tower event, with shininess and IVs fixed at that moment. Because the roll happens at creation, re-encountering the same roamer always gives the same result. Running away and tracking it down again will not re-roll it. Defeating or catching a roamer takes it off the map, and it will not come back on its own. Entering the Hall of Fame as Kanto Champion respawns them: the caught flags are cleared and Raikou and Entei are created fresh, with new IVs and shininess. The Kanto roamer is recreated at the same time. Beating the Kanto League again repeats this, so it is the repeatable way to hunt them. Before that point, save ahead of the Burned Tower event and re-trigger it to re-roll. You can track a roamer's current location from your Pokedex.
Items
Where can I find this HM?
All HM locations are listed on Items & TMs .
Gameplay
What's the best way to gain EXP before the Johto Elite Four?

There is a Lucky Egg lying on the ground on Route 47, which connects Cianwood City to the Safari Zone and Route 48. It increases EXP gain by 1.5x while held. Descend through the caves to the bottom until you can surf, then go up either accessible waterfall to reach it. A Lucky Egg can also be held by a wild Chansey, but only rarely. Chansey itself appears in the grass on Route 47 at a 40% rate during the day and is worth a lot of EXP, so it is a good place to grind either way.
Items
Does the Exp Share S stack with the Exp Share key item?

No. While the Exp Share key item is switched on it replaces the Exp Share S entirely - every healthy party member is already sharing EXP, so holding one adds nothing. The Exp Share S only does something when the key item is switched off.

Key item ON: the Pokemon that fought split 2/3 of the battle's EXP between them, and every other healthy party member earns 28% of it, held item or not. Defeat a Pokemon worth 100 EXP with one Pokemon and a full party and the one that fought earns 66 while the other five earn 28 each. (If it is the only healthy Pokemon in your party it earns the full 100 instead - no sharing penalty when there is nobody to share with.) Key item OFF: half the EXP is split between the Pokemon that fought and half between the Pokemon holding an Exp Share S, so 50 each in a one-on-one battle.
Technical
My game crashes after the GameFreak text, or goes black and never loads.
MyBoy and gpSP will not work. If the game crashes right after the copyright screen you need a different emulator.
We make GBA games - if they run on original hardware, that is what we are aiming for. Check the recommended emulator list in the downloads post.
Technical
The game got updated. How do I transfer my save to the new version?

Take your character to the nearest Pokemon Center and save. Back up your save file, then rename your original to match the new ROM's name. Start the new ROM, confirm your name appears, then leave the Pokemon Center before doing anything else. That updates everything.
Save files transfer (.sav, .srm, .fla). Save states do not.
Technical
Where are all the cheats? Why won't Emerald GameShark codes work?
Cheats and save editors go against the design philosophy of the game. In v1.2 one concession was made for Nuzlocke mode by adding Infinite Rare Candies, and no more will be added.
Codes found online or intended for vanilla Emerald are not condoned and will not work. Issues reported by people using cheats, or patches from Heart & Soul impersonators, will not be supported.
Other
Will Hoenn be added to the game?
There are no plans to include Hoenn in the official release. The game is open source, so community members are welcome to make their own forks on GitHub.
Other
I want to mod the game myself, or get help with my own version. Where do I start?
Start in the how-to-romhack channel on the Discord, where people are collaborating on their own projects.

features.title: Setting Expectations
rows: Heart & Soul was designed as a traditional Pokémon experience, akin to the main-series games. It is not a difficulty hack. The challenge settings are a bonus, but the game is not balanced around them and will not be in the future.

Heart & Soul stands on the shoulders of giants. I am not an artist, so much of the art and some of the code for this project was drawn from open source assets. I did my best to credit all sources below and in the game credits, but if you find any that I missed, please let me know in the Heart & Soul Discord .
Heart & Soul has been rigorously playtested, (shoutout to the playtesters) but there still may be some small bugs. If you find any, please report them to the Heart & Soul Discord .
Heart & Soul is not intended to be 1:1 with GSC or HGSS. A lot of it is. But some differences are intentional.

features.title: Features
rows: Generation 1–3 Pokémon, plus their later-gen evolutions (excluding the Regis)
Full Johto story and Kanto postgame from HGSS, including the Kimono Girls and Eusine
Following Pokémon
Physical/Special split is toggleable
Overworld background Pokémon allow you to easily see the notable encounters on each route
Overworld background Pokémon in cities, towns, or areas with no encounters are just for the vibes
Day/Night system with variable encounters
Dynamic overworld palettes
HGSS music
Battle Frontier, Trainer Hill, and Trainer Tents from modern Emerald
Highly varied trainer teams and encounters, based on Crystal Legacy
Pokémon that can learn an HM do not need to have learned it to use the HM field move
Timekeeping does not track days of the week; everything is progression based
16 Gym leader rematches
Two Safari Zones
Unique surfing Pokémon sprites
Customizable shiny rate
Fairy type is toggleable
AutoRun and FastSurf are toggleable
Quick run from wild battles using button combination
Ball prompts for quick catching

features.title: 2.0 Features
rows: Rebuilt the game and all features on pokeemerald-expansion. This means saves from before 2.0 are not compatible with versions after 2.0.
Restored Surf and Bike music, with the option to disable
Abilities up to Gen 9, including Hidden Abilities
Items from up to Gen 9 available, including Shiny Charm (not all items)
Randomizer has all mons Gen 1–9
Hidden Items + Itemfinder
Overhauled Kanto maps and tilesets
Kanto rematch trainers
Kanto in-game trades
All PokéGear rematches from GSC (and some new ones), including gift items, with the option to disable
Full PokéGear Radio with all channels from Crystal (and some new ones)
PokéGear Condition menu
All 92 HGSS TMs
New postgame content
Kurt's Berry Balls boost catch rate by custom-defined type affinity if more impactful than the vanilla boost
GB Player Key Item to toggle Gen 2 music and sounds
Removed all bike reaction time puzzles
Added ice Path boulder puzzle
Mom's Savings System
Voltorb Flip
Entei, Raikou, and the new Kanto roamer are all independent
Choose one Lati to roam Kanto. The other will be at Southern Island.
Roamers no longer intentionally avoid the player's route
Added a sound cue and animation when the player enters the same route as a roamer
Added a clock to the start menu
Added Optional Bonus Content: TELEPORTER, accessible from the Kanto postgame
Room Decoration (dolls only) in New Bark Town
Spiky-eared Pichu event in Viridian
Added Optional Bonus Content: ISLES, accessible from the Kanto postgame
Slowpokes grow their tails back when you beat the league
Tutors and trades can utilize your PC Pokémon
Added Optional Bonus Content: SINJOH, accessible from the Kanto postgame
Can fly to more routes and Pokémon Centers
Rocket takeover only happens after the 7th badge, no matter where you get it
Buffed the Kimono Girls
Various UI/UX improvements, including Shiny Markers for colorblindness accessibility and shiny-hunting QOL
New Battle Backgrounds: Cave ponds, snowy routes, snowy mountain, snowy cave, volcano cave, new beach

features.title: Differences from GSC / HGSS
rows: Level curve is greatly improved
Apricons are replaced with berries, including to be made into unique Pokéballs by Kurt
Swarms are replaced with a 5% Hoenn encounter on each route in Kanto, which can be boosted via the Hoenn Sound radio channel
Ruins of Alph back room requirements are slightly altered
No Pokéathlon dome
Modern Emerald Battle Frontier and Battle Tents
Unlike vanilla Emerald, "Level 50" will set any Pokémon level 1–100 to level 50, and "Open Level" will accept any Pokémon as-is

breeding.title: Egg groups
rows: Gen 8's egg group additions are applied.
Setting: P_UPDATED_EGG_GROUPS = GEN_LATEST (Gen 9)

breeding.title: Vivillon patterns
rows: The Scatterbug, Spewpa and Vivillon line always breeds into the Fancy pattern.
Setting: P_SCATTERBUG_LINE_FORM_BREED = SPECIES_SCATTERBUG_FANCY

breeding.title: Poke Ball
rows: The egg inherits a parent's Poke Ball ; the father can pass it down too, as long as he's the same species as the mother.
Setting: P_BALL_INHERITING = GEN_LATEST (Gen 9)

breeding.title: TM moves
rows: Fathers do not pass down TM moves.
Setting: P_TM_INHERITANCE = GEN_LATEST (Gen 9)

breeding.title: Egg moves
rows: Either parent can pass down Egg Moves.
Setting: P_MOTHER_EGG_MOVE_INHERITANCE = GEN_LATEST (Gen 9)

breeding.title: Nature
rows: A parent holding an Everstone always passes down its Nature.
Setting: P_NATURE_INHERITANCE = GEN_LATEST (Gen 9)

breeding.title: Ability
rows: 80% chance to pass down a regular Ability. Either parent can pass it, including when bred with Ditto. Hidden Abilities are not inherited.
Setting: P_ABILITY_INHERITANCE = GEN_LATEST (Gen 9)

breeding.title: IVs
rows: 3 of the baby's six IVs are inherited at random from its parents; the rest are random. A parent holding a Destiny Knot raises that to 5.
Setting: src/daycare.c = InheritIVs

breeding.title: Power items
rows: A parent holding a Power item ( Power Weight , Power Bracer and so on) always passes down that item's IV, using up one of the inherited slots. Both parents holding one means one of them is picked at random.
Setting: src/daycare.c = HOLD_EFFECT_POWER_ITEM

breeding.title: What level they hatch at
rows: Eggs hatch at level 1.
Setting: P_EGG_HATCH_LEVEL = GEN_LATEST (Gen 9)

breeding.title: How long an egg takes
rows: Egg cycles use the original (longer) step counts.
Setting: P_EGG_CYCLE_LENGTH = GEN_3 (Gen 3)
